expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)
question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
rendered:
According to the text, after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS at 1C rates. The whole electrode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), which is an impressive mass-specific performance especially with the moderate loading of 35 wt % active sulfur.

The ratio of the cathode capacity to the whole electrode capacity is 306 mAh/gS / 87 mAh/g = 3.52. This ratio implies that the sulfur share of the electrode is approximately 35 wt % / 3.52 = 9.9 wt %.

The paper states that the sulfur content is 35 wt %. This means that after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers a capacity that corresponds to about 28.2% of the sulfur content, assuming the same capacity per gram of sulfur as at the beginning of the test.
